key_insight: Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs) generate text designed to strongly activate a chosen direction inside a language model. This moves interpretation beyond examples that happen to exist in a scanned corpus.
problem_solved: Searching a fixed text corpus can miss examples that reveal what a residual stream direction represents, limiting how well researchers can interpret model internals.
method: Provide a MAEM with a direction from a subject language model’s residual stream.
Use the MAEM to generate text exemplars intended to strongly activate that direction.
Optimize for cosine alignment with the supplied direction; the provided abstract is truncated before the full objective is specified.
impact: This approach could help interpret model representations by producing targeted examples rather than relying solely on corpus search. The provided excerpt does not include results establishing its effectiveness or coverage.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: residual stream direction → MAEM → generated text exemplar.
Side-by-side comparison: searching a fixed corpus versus generating targeted examples.

Conceptual activation heatmap linking generated text tokens to the selected direction.
paper_title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
paper_authors: Celeste De Schamphelaere, Juan J. Vazquez, Ari Spiesberger, Tomáš Gavenčiak, Gavin Leech
